stem.text: An open-top storage bin is made from a square sheet of plastic 36 inches on a side by cutting a square of side x from each corner and folding up the sides. The storage bin can be at most 1 inch tall. Find the largest possible volume of the storage bin, in cubic inches.

worked_solution.text: The storage bin has height x and a square base of side \( 36 - 2 x \), so its volume is \( V(x) = x\left(36 - 2 x\right)^{2} \).
The cut must be positive, less than half the sheet, and at most 1, so the domain is \( 0 < x \le 1 \).
\( V'(x) = 12 \left(x - 18\right) \left(x - 6\right) \), which is zero at \( x = 6 \) and \( x = 18 \); only \( x = 6 \) lies strictly inside the sheet.
The critical point \( x = 6 \) is beyond the height limit, and \( V'(x) > 0 \) for every x in \( 0 < x \le 1 \), so V is increasing there and is largest at the right endpoint \( x = 1 \).
The largest volume is \( V(1) = 1\left(34\right)^{2} = 1156 \) cubic inches.

options.derivation: the side of the cut square, where the maximum occurs, reported instead of the volume
the shorter side of the base at the optimum reported instead of the volume
the height limit left out of the domain, so the critical point x = 6 is used
